title: Sou
edition: First edition, 300 numbered copies, signed by the artist

description.main: Koji Takiguchi's first book, Sou (窓, window), is a photographic diary of his family over a few years in which his wife's parents die, their son is born and the household cat dies. Little Big Man published it in 2014 in an edition of 300 signed and numbered copies.
description.extended:
Koji Takiguchi's first book, Sou (窓, window), is a photographic diary of his family over a few years in which his wife's parents die, their son is born and the household cat dies.

The sequence opens at the hospital bed of Takiguchi's mother-in-law in the last days of her cancer. These are the pictures that won him the New Cosmos of Photography co-Grand Prize in 2004, selected by Nobuyoshi Araki. It follows her widower's decline, the birth of Takiguchi's son, the death of the cat Ponta and his father-in-law's final illness. Between these runs he lays old snapshots of his in-laws, and of himself and his wife, over pressed flowers kept in the family. Windows recur throughout, in curtained light and views out of hospital rooms. Little Big Man produced the book in 2014 as a 116-page softcover with about 90 photographs under a transparent dust jacket, in an edition of 300 numbered copies signed by the artist. Araki brushed the single character on the cover. An interview with the critic Dan Abbe closes the book.

Takiguchi (b. 1977, Shizuoka) studied design at Tokyo University of the Arts and works across photography, animation and painting, designing his own books. Sou is the only title of his from Nick Haymes's Little Big Man, whose Japanese list also includes Keizo Kitajima, Motoyuki Daifu and Araki.
description.artist_bio: Koji Takiguchi (滝口浩史) was born in 1977 in Shizuoka Prefecture. He graduated from the Department of Design at Tokyo University of the Arts in 2001 and completed a master's degree there in 2019. In 2004 his series Hazama, photographs of his wife and her dying mother, received an Excellence Award and the co-Grand Prize at Canon's New Cosmos of Photography, selected by Nobuyoshi Araki. He also works in animation and painting and designs his own photobooks; Japanese dealers list an ongoing self-published series, Neko no tsumetogi.
description.exhibition_context: A solo show titled 窓-SOU was held at Nikon Salon Juna 21 (Shinjuku) in 2008, according to Canon's listing summarised by a web search; not independently verified.
